timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: RAM is just short-term memory, right? Like a scratchpad?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Correct, but a scratchpad where every secret you've ever typed is written in permanent ink for a few seconds.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: Wait, passwords are stored in RAM? That sounds dangerous.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Every time you log in, your password travels through RAM. And malware can read it directly.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So if I shut down my computer, the data is gone, right?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Not necessarily. Cold boot attacks freeze RAM to preserve data for minutes after power-off.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: That's terrifying. Is there any defense?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: DDR5 has on-die encryption. But most systems still use DDR4 without it. And RAM scraping attacks bypass the OS entirely.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: What about memory forensics? Do investigators use this?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Absolutely. A RAM dump can reveal running processes, network connections, encryption keys, and clipboard contents.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So RAM is basically a crime scene that nobody cleans up?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: A crime scene that auto-destructs in milliseconds but can be frozen in time with the right tools.
